sections.content: You know *ponerse*, *quedarse*, *volverse* and *hacerse* from B1 Unit 25, and *llegar a ser* from B1 Unit 39. To choose, ask what kind of change it is. A quick, passing reaction: *ponerse*. The state left after an event: *quedarse*. A lasting change in character or in a situation: *volverse*. A profession or choice: *hacerse*. A complete change into something new: *convertirse en* or *transformarse en*. The high point of a long road: *llegar a ser*. At B2 you also meet a shorter way for some of them: one verb that carries the change inside it, such as *palidecer* (= *ponerse pálido*) or *enrojecer* (= *ponerse rojo*). It sounds a little more written, and it is shorter.

items.spanish: Al oír el precio, mi madre palideció.
items.english: On hearing the price, my mother turned pale.

items.spanish: Con el comercio, el pueblo se enriqueció.
items.english: With trade, the town became rich.

items.spanish: El público enmudeció cuando apareció el cantante.
items.english: The audience fell silent when the singer appeared.

sections.content: Mind the *se*: *palidecer*, *enrojecer* and *enmudecer* have none, while *enriquecerse* and *empobrecerse* keep it. If you are not sure which to use, the two-word form (*se puso pálido*) is always right.
